what_its_for: This eye drop is used to treat Demodex blepharitis, which is an eyelid condition caused by tiny mites called Demodex. These mites live at the base of your eyelashes and can cause your eyelids to become red, irritated, itchy, and crusty. Lotilaner works by killing these mites to help clear up the infection and relieve your symptoms.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using this medicine. Tilt your head back and gently pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket. Hold the dropper above your eye and squeeze one drop into the pocket of your lower eyelid. Try not to let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, or any other surface to keep it clean. After putting in the drop, gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting your contacts back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each different eye medication.
dosing: Use one drop in each affected eye twice a day, morning and evening, for 6 weeks. Try to use the drops at the same times each day to help you remember. Always use it exactly as your doctor prescribed and complete the full 6-week course of treatment, even if your eyes start to feel better sooner.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the eye drops as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular routine. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the eye drops. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Throw away any unused solution 60 days after opening the bottle, even if there is still medicine left inside.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the drops and cause an eye infection. Do not wear contact lenses while your eyes are still red or irritated. Avoid rubbing your eyes after applying the drops. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right away if your vision is temporarily blurry after using the drops — wait until your vision clears before doing these activities.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience any of the following: severe eye pain or increased redness, new or worsening vision changes, signs of an eye infection such as increased discharge or swelling, an allergic reaction including rash, itching, or difficulty breathing, or if your symptoms do not improve after completing the full 6-week treatment course. Also call your doctor if the dropper tip accidentally touches a contaminated surface.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in your symptoms, such as less redness, itching, and irritation, within the first few weeks of treatment. However, it is very important to complete the full 6 weeks of treatment as directed, even if you feel better early. The mites need the full course of treatment to be fully eliminated. Many patients see the best results by the end of the 6-week treatment period.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully studied. This medicine has not been studied in children under 18 years of age. Older adults can generally use this medicine safely, but should follow the same instructions as other adults. If you have other eye conditions or have recently had eye surgery, let your doctor know before starting this treatment.
